title: Canonical site Hom restriction maps and comparison square
statement:
Use the ordinary unbounded etale and pro-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their derived internal Homs [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], comparison inverse images [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and the canonical inverse-image square comparisons [def-per-site-comparison-pullback-data]. Monoidal and closed structures have their usual meaning [def-sfb-monoidal-category]; the site comparison map $\beta$ is the specified evaluation transpose [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison].

For an exact additive strong monoidal left adjoint $G:C\to D$ between closed braided Grothendieck abelian categories with functorial flat resolutions, suppose $G$ preserves flat objects. Define its monoidal structure on the termwise derived functor by transporting the residue-derived monoidal structure along the canonical isomorphism $LG\cong D(G)$. This is the construction denoted $m_G$ below, not an arbitrary monoidal structure.

Let $f:Y\to X$ be a scheme morphism, and let $B$ be a symmetric closed monoidal Grothendieck abelian coefficient category with monoidal preadditivity and functorial flat resolutions, of object size $u+2$ and morphism size $u+1$ for schemes of size $u$. Write $r_e=D(f_e^*)$, $r_p=D(f_p^*)$, and $F_X=D(\nu_X^*)$, $F_Y=D(\nu_Y^*)$. Define $\theta:r_eF_Y\cong F_Xr_p$ by deriving the ordinary canonical inverse-image square, with the canonical derived composition identifications on either side. For specified monoidal structures $m_e,m_p$ on $r_e,r_p$, define
$$h_e(K,M):r_eH_{e,X}(K,M)\to H_{e,Y}(r_eK,r_eM),\qquad h_p(P,Q):r_pH_{p,X}(P,Q)\to H_{p,Y}(r_pP,r_pQ)$$
as the transposes of restricted evaluation using $m_e,m_p$. When $\nu_X^*,\nu_Y^*$ preserve flat objects, define the restriction assertion at $K,M\in D(X_e,B)$ to be that $h_e(K,M)$ and $h_p(F_XK,F_XM)$ are invertible and that
$$F_Y(h_e(K,M))\,\beta^Y_{r_eK,r_eM}\,H_{p,Y}(\theta_K^{-1},\theta_M)=\theta_{H_{e,X}(K,M)}\,r_p(\beta^X_{K,M})\,h_p(F_XK,F_XM).$$
Composition here is read left to right. The abstract restriction-square assertion is the same conjunction for any four categories, internal-Hom-shaped bifunctors $H,H_1,G,G_1$, functors $F,F_1,r_e,r_p$, natural isomorphism $\theta:r_eF_1\cong Fr_p$, and families $\beta,\beta_1,h_e,h_p$ with the displayed types; it asserts the same two invertibilities and equation, without choosing any of these maps.

For a finite commutative ring $A$, $X$ a scheme and $U\in X_{\mathrm{et}}$, define the structure arrow to be $U\to X$ itself, the two restriction functors to be $D((U\to X)_e^*)$ and $D((U\to X)_p^*)$ on ordinary constant-$A$ modules, and their square to be the preceding $\theta$ for $B=\operatorname{Mod}_A$. Give both restriction functors the structure $m_G$ above (the pro-etale pullback preserves flat objects since $U\to X$ is weakly etale). Define the two fixed-coefficient internal-Hom restriction maps by the preceding evaluation transposes with these structures. These are definitions of actual canonical maps and of a predicate on them; no restriction equation or invertibility theorem is asserted.

def siteHomRestrictionAssertion
    (B : Type (u + 2)) [Category.{u + 1} B] [Abelian B]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} B] [MonoidalCategory B]
    [MonoidalPreadditive B] [SymmetricCategory B] [MonoidalClosed B]
    [Abelian.HasFunctorialFlatResolution B]
    {Y X : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [(comparisonUpperStar B X).PreservesFlat]
    [(comparisonUpperStar B Y).PreservesFlat]
    (m_e : (Etale.upperStar B f).mapDerivedCategory.Monoidal)
    (m_p : (upperStar B f).mapDerivedCategory.Monoidal)
    (K M : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology B)) : Prop
